# Data Preprocessing and Normalization

Also called: Volume Preprocessing, Data Normalization, HU Normalization

## Overview
This family encompasses methods that prepare volumetric data for compression or rendering by ensuring data integrity, standardizing physical units, and mapping value ranges to canonical intervals. It solves the problem of heterogeneous input formats and physical scales that hinder efficient compression or consistent visualization. It differs from sibling methods like [Sparse structures](5-sparse-structures.md) or [Value compression](6-value-compression.md) by operating prior to topological organization or bit-depth reduction, focusing instead on format compatibility and physical correctness [S1, unofficial][S3, S4, unofficial][S6][S7, S8, unofficial].

## Shared principles
Not given in the sources.

## Subtopics

### [Volume Normalization](1823-volume-normalization.md)
Volume Normalization scales a volume tensor to the range $[0, 1]$ while preserving constant positive masks as full foreground ($1.0$). It is chosen when a generic, statistical range mapping is required for rendering or compression pipelines. It differs from [Volume Utility Functions](2677-volume-utility-functions.md) by applying a global min-max transform rather than specific physical unit conversions or spatial resampling.

### [Volume Utility Functions](2677-volume-utility-functions.md)
Volume Utility Functions prepare volumetric data for the [Compression](4-compression.md) pipeline by addressing distinct aspects of data integrity and range mapping [Parent]. They handle tensor dimensionality alignment via `make_nd`, physical unit normalization via `normalize_hounsfield`, spatial resampling via `normalize_voxel_scale`, and memory/layout corrections. Unlike [Sparse structures](5-sparse-structures.md) which organize data topology, or [Value compression](6-value-compression.md) which reduces bit-depth, these utilities ensure data integrity and format compatibility before compression or rendering occurs.

### [Dataset Preprocessing (DeepLesion)](7228-dataset-preprocessing-deeplesion.md)
This method prepares tomographic images from the DeepLesion dataset for training generative models by converting raw scanner data into standardized Hounsfield Units (HU), segmenting the patient anatomy from background noise, and normalizing spatial resolution. It differs from generic [Volume Normalization](1823-volume-normalization.md) by using a specific anatomical threshold (-9050 HU) to define the region of interest rather than global statistical scaling, and from [Volume Utility Functions](2677-volume-utility-functions.md) by enforcing a strict minimum output dimension (256x256).

### Density Range Restriction and Ramp Function
#### definition
- [S1, unofficial] A preprocessing function applied to volume data to restrict the range of density values, improving compression ratio by removing irrelevant data and avoiding discontinuities that generate high frequencies.
#### step
- [S1, unofficial] Apply function $T$ to each density value: if density $\le d_1$, set density $= 0$; if density $\ge d_3$, set density $= 0$; if $d_1 \le \text{density} \le d_2$, set density $= (\text{density} - d_1) \times d_2 / (d_2 - d_1)$; if $d_3 \le \text{density} \le d_4$, set density $= (d_3 - \text{density}) \times d_4 / (d_4 - d_3)$.
- [S1, unofficial] Normalize models with histograms outside the $[0, 255]$ range to achieve the same output value range after applying $T$.
#### parameter
- [S1, unofficial] $d_1, d_2, d_3, d_4$: Threshold parameters defining the density range $[d_2, d_3]$ to keep intact and the ramps $[d_1, d_2]$ and $[d_3, d_4]$ to avoid discontinuities.

## Background
The concept of restricting density ranges to improve compression ratios was introduced in the context of mobile volumetric medical image visualization [S1, unofficial]. The specific DeepLesion preprocessing pipeline is designed for training generative models on tomographic data [S1, unofficial]. General volume utility functions for dimensionality and unit normalization are standard practices in medical imaging pipelines [S1, unofficial][S3, S4, unofficial][S6][S7, S8, unofficial].
